::: {#exr-miller-deriv-log-simplify}
#### Derivative after logarithmic simplification

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.4.

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = \log(4x) - \log(2x)$$

for $x > 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-log-simplify}
Simplify before differentiating using the quotient property of logarithms:

$$f(x) = \log(4x) - \log(2x) = \log\paren{\frac{4x}{2x}} = \log 2$$

Because $\log 2$ is constant with respect to $x$, the constant rule (@thm-deriv-const) gives:

$$f'(x) = 0$$

*Remark:* While one could apply the chain rule separately to each term ($\frac{4}{4x} - \frac{2}{2x} = \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{x} = 0$), simplifying algebraically first is faster and prevents arithmetic errors.
:::
